rules.title: Password hashed with a fast digest
rules.description: General-purpose digests are built to be fast, which is exactly wrong for passwords - a modern GPU tries billions of candidates per second.
rules.remediation: Use argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt with a per-password salt and a tuned work factor.

rules.title: MD5 or SHA-1 used for integrity or signing
rules.description: MD5 and SHA-1 both have practical collision attacks; neither is acceptable where collision resistance matters.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256 or better. If this is a non-security checksum, say so in a comment and suppress the rule.

rules.title: Block cipher in ECB mode
rules.description: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks to identical ciphertext blocks, so structure leaks straight through the encryption.
rules.remediation: Use an authenticated mode: AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a unique nonce per message.

rules.title: Hardcoded or zero IV / nonce
rules.description: Reusing an IV under the same key destroys the security of CBC and is catastrophic for CTR and GCM - it leaks plaintext XOR and, for GCM, the authentication key.
rules.remediation: Generate a fresh random IV per message with a CSPRNG and store it alongside the ciphertext.

rules.title: Non-cryptographic RNG used for a secret
rules.description: These PRNGs are predictable from a handful of outputs. A token generated from one can be reproduced by an attacker.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.description: Without verification, any network position can present its own certificate and read or rewrite the traffic. TLS with verification off is plaintext with extra CPU cost.
rules.remediation: Verify certificates. For an internal CA, add the CA bundle rather than disabling the check.

rules.title: Obsolete TLS/SSL protocol version pinned
rules.description: TLS below 1.2 has known attacks (POODLE, BEAST, downgrade) and is rejected by current clients.
rules.remediation: Require TLS 1.2 as a floor, 1.3 where available.

rules.title: Broken cipher (DES, 3DES, RC4, Blowfish)
rules.description: These ciphers have small block sizes or practical key-recovery attacks and are no longer considered secure.

rules.title: JWT verification accepting alg=none or unverified decode
rules.description: Decoding a JWT without verifying its signature means the client decides what the claims say - including which user they are.
rules.remediation: Always verify with an explicit algorithm allowlist and the correct key. jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=['RS256']).

rules.title: Secret compared with == instead of a constant-time check
rules.description: A short-circuiting comparison leaks how many leading bytes matched, which is enough to forge a signature byte by byte over many requests.

rules.title: RSA/DSA key smaller than 2048 bits
rules.description: 1024-bit RSA is below every current guideline and considered factorable by a well-resourced adversary.
rules.remediation: Use 3072-bit RSA, or move to Ed25519/ECDSA P-256.

rules.title: Hardcoded salt for key derivation
rules.description: A shared salt means identical passwords produce identical hashes, which makes precomputation worthwhile again.
rules.remediation: Generate a random salt per record and store it with the hash.
